name: Youthmaxxing

lead: Youthmaxxing is the practice of trying to look younger for longer. People use it to keep smooth skin, a full head of hair and a fresh-faced look into their 30s and 40s, and some aim to keep a boyish appearance.

In practice the term covers a bundle of habits that dermatologists also discuss, such as sleep, sun protection and skincare, alongside more unusual ideas that circulate on forums. Little of the community's wider list has been tested as a package.

paras: Forum users describe routines built around sleep and napping, stress reduction, facial skincare, avoiding the sun, hair preservation, lifting and diet. Some add collagen-oriented foods such as bone broth, and some experiment with compounds. Posters present timelines from months to years.

The ordinary habits carry little risk. Some posters mention substances (for example minoxidil on the face, or growth-hormone secretagogues) that carry their own side effects and are covered on their own pages. Claims such as semen retention extending youth have not been studied.

angle.text: Youthmaxxers combine daily habits and skincare to keep skin smooth and hair full, aiming for a younger appearance at a given age. The benefit comes from the individual components rather than from the label.

lead: Youthmaxxing is a term from looksmaxxing forums for efforts to preserve, or visually recreate, a younger-looking face, skin and hair. It sits at the intersection of skincare, hair retention, sleep, fitness and lifestyle, and belongs to the softmaxxing end of looksmaxxing, which Wikipedia describes as covering low-intensity methods such as skincare, grooming and fitness.[1][2][3]

People pursue it so that wrinkles, nasolabial folds and thinning hair appear later, aiming for what one poster called a boyish look into their 40s.[2][4] The strategies listed in forum threads range from familiar ones (sleep, stress control, skincare, avoiding sun exposure) to unconventional ones (raw meat, nofap, time in nature, even thought control).[1][4] Of these, sun avoidance has the most published research behind it: dermatology sources describe ultraviolet exposure as the main cause of visible facial skin ageing, and a randomised trial in Australia found less skin ageing in people who used sunscreen daily.[5][6][7]

The wiki records the wider list as community beliefs. No published study has tested the combined youthmaxxing approach, although individual components such as sun protection and topical tretinoin have their own research literature.[5][6]

paras: The term is used loosely. One thread describes a three-part approach of sleep (with regular naps), staying calm to limit stress hormones, and facial skincare, which the poster called the most important part, with nofap, avoiding drugs and alcohol, and avoiding the sun as auxiliary measures.[4] Another poster, aged 24, started a thread out of concern about early signs of aging and a wish for wrinkle-free skin and a full head of hair.[2]

Related forum vocabulary follows the same suffix pattern: sleepmaxxing, naturemaxxing, skinmaxxing and thoughtmaxxing appear in a single list of youth-preservation ideas.[1] Looksmaxxing itself, per Wikipedia, grew from manosphere forums in the 2010s and spread on TikTok in the 2020s, and its softmaxxing branch covers skincare, grooming and fitness.[3]

sections.h: Beliefs and methods in the community
paras: Posters list sleep optimisation, avoiding sun, nature exposure, air-pollution avoidance, skincare, jaw and palate expansion (with the idea that folds and fat-pad sag stem from facial recession), raw meat, and semen retention.[1][4] Some suggestions are plainly tongue-in-cheek, and others in the same threads dismiss them as engagement bait.[1]

One poster reported that facial minoxidil, used to grow a beard, coincided with lower skin quality and early nasolabial folds, and attributed this to effects on collagen.[2] Replies suggested supplements, a better diet and growth-hormone secretagogues instead, and noted most people show few signs of aging at 24.[2]

Hair preservation also sits under the heading: the original poster in one thread names a full, healthy head of hair alongside smooth skin as the two goals.[2] Training is mentioned as part of the wider package, with the same poster describing lifting as an earlier looks project.[2]

sections.h: What skin and ageing research reports
paras: Dermatology references describe photoageing as skin change from long-term UVA and UVB exposure, showing as wrinkles, pigment changes, roughness and laxity, with UV activating enzymes that break down collagen.[5] The same page describes sun protection as the primary preventive measure and topical tretinoin as the most effective treatment, supported by several randomised trials.[5]

Wikipedia's sunscreen entry notes a 2013 study of about 900 light-skinned people in Australia in which daily broad-spectrum sunscreen users had smoother, more resilient skin after four and a half years than discretionary users.[7][6] It also says cortisol degrades collagen and accelerates skin ageing, which proponents of stress control cite in the same breath as sleep and calm.[8] Wikipedia's skin article notes that skin thins and loses volume and elasticity with age.[8]

Skincare routines, sunscreen, retinoids, sleep optimisation and hair-retention treatments each have their own entries on the wiki. Youthmaxxing is the umbrella label some forum users apply to combining them with the aim of appearing younger than their age.

No studies found for youthmaxxing as a combined approach. A randomised trial of 903 adults under 55 in Nambour, Australia, compared daily with discretionary SPF 15 or higher sunscreen over about 4.5 years and found 24 percent lower skin ageing in the daily group (relative odds 0.76, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.98); beta-carotene had no overall effect, and the authors noted some missing data and modest statistical power.[6] That trial addressed one component only.

lore.intro: Youthmaxxing threads on looksmax.org combine skincare and lifestyle tips with speculative ideas.[1][2][4]

claims.claim: Skincare, sleep and low stress keep you looking younger
Facial minoxidil can lower skin quality
Avoiding the sun keeps skin looking young
Raw meat and bone broth slow ageing of cells or boost collagen

timeline.event: Franz Greiter introduces the sun protection factor (SPF) rating for sunscreens.[7]
Nambour sunscreen trial begins measuring skin microtopography; follow-up runs to 1996.[6]
Annals of Internal Medicine publishes the Nambour randomised trial, reporting less skin ageing with daily sunscreen.[6]
Looksmaxxing terminology spreads from forums such as PUAHate and Lookism.net, per Wikipedia.[3]
Looksmaxxing becomes popular on TikTok, including softmaxxing topics such as skincare.[3]
